# tissue_mast_vital (Resource)

A Mast vital: a channel that expects a beat on a schedule and pages when one is late. Send a beat by requesting its `url`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Expects a beat after the 03:00 backup, and pages if none arrives by 03:30.
resource "tissue_mast_vital" "backup" {
  name        = "nightly-backup"
  schedule    = "0 3 * * *"
  schedule_tz = "America/Los_Angeles"
  grace_secs  = 1800
  host        = "db1"
}

# A job that should check in every five minutes.
resource "tissue_mast_vital" "queue" {
  name           = "queue-worker"
  period_secs    = 300
  grace_secs     = 120
  fail_threshold = 2
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name shown in the app and on every notification. Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and single spaces, at most 32 characters. Renaming keeps the URL.

### Optional

- `ack_timeout_min` (Number) Minutes an acknowledged incident stays quiet before paging again. `0` never re-pages.
- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the vital is archived. An archived vital takes no sends and its URL answers 404 until it's restored. Leave it unset to follow the app, where people archive and restore; set it to `false` to restore one archived there. Restoring counts against the plan's channel limit again.
- `canary_url` (String) An http or https URL Mast fetches to check the sender is still alive. Empty turns it off.
- `dedupe_window_secs` (Number) Repeats of one message inside this many seconds fold into one. Default 300.
- `default_priority` (String) Priority of a send that doesn't name one: `quiet`, `normal`, `loud` or `page`. The server's default is `normal`.
- `escalate_after_secs` (Number) Seconds before an unacknowledged page escalates. `0` turns it off.
- `expire_secs` (Number) How long an unacknowledged page keeps repeating. Default 3600.
- `fail_threshold` (Number) Missed beats in a row before it pages. Default 1.
- `grace_secs` (Number) How late a beat can be before the vital pages. A `schedule` needs it above 0.
- `host` (String) The machine the job runs on, shown with the page. Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- `max_duration_secs` (Number) Longest a run between `/start` and its beat may take. `0` is no limit.
- `max_priority` (String) The highest priority a send can ask for. A new vital can start at `quiet`, `normal` or `loud` (the default). Raising it to `page` is done in the Mast app, on the owner's phone, and after create the value can only be changed there. Leave it unset to follow the app, or set it to what the app shows.
- `paused` (Boolean) Takes the vital off watch. Leave it unset if people pause it from the app.
- `period_secs` (Number) Seconds between beats for an interval vital. `0` when the vital runs on a `schedule`.
- `policy_id` (String) The escalation policy pages on this vital follow, `po_...`. Set it to `""` to detach one; leaving the argument out keeps whatever the app has.
- `quiet_end` (Number) End of the quiet window, in minutes past midnight, or `-1` for none.
- `quiet_start` (Number) Start of a daily quiet window, in minutes past midnight, or `-1` for none.
- `quiet_tz` (String) Time zone the quiet window is read in: an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin`, or an offset such as `+0530`. Empty is UTC.
- `repeat_secs` (Number) How often an unacknowledged page repeats. Default 120.
- `schedule` (String) A five-field crontab for when the watched job starts, such as `0 3 * * *`.
- `schedule_tz` (String) Time zone the schedule is read in, as for `quiet_tz`. Empty is UTC.
- `smart_early_warn` (Boolean) Warn quietly when beats start arriving later than usual, before the vital is late.
- `sound` (String) The sound a push plays: `default`, `bleep`, `chirp`, `klaxon`, `pager` or `rising`. Empty means whatever the priority plays.
- `storm_threshold` (Number) Sends inside the storm window past which Mast holds the rest. Default 20.
- `storm_window_secs` (Number) Length of the storm window. Default 300.
- `vital_priority` (String) Priority of the page a late vital sends. Default `loud`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the vital was made.
- `id` (String) The vital id, `mc_...`.
- `url` (String, Sensitive) The ingest URL. It carries the key, so anyone holding it can send to this vital.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import tissue_mast_vital.backup nightly-backup
```
